topics.topic: Kernel handling of refused operation-node trace writes after possible external effects
questions: What happens when the store refuses the trace record for an operation-node execution, especially after the service may have applied the operation?
What must the kernel do when the store refuses the trace record for an operation-node execution, especially when the external operation may already have taken effect?
What happens when the store refuses the trace record for an operation-node execution, especially after the service may already have acted?

quotes:
Everything a resume or a restart needs is in the store before it is acted on:
   records of concluded attempts, decided approvals, and in-flight attempts before
   their request (K-17).

On start, before the surface accepts a request, the kernel turns every
`in_flight` EffectAttempt into `unknown` (A11 rule 4) and then derives every
run that has not ended — `running`, `awaiting_approval` or `pending` — again
from its records, oldest first in store order, rewriting a stored status or
waiting point that lags them (a decided approval, a resolved attempt, an
outcome whose run change was lost), and advances, as the
kernel actor, every run that derivation leaves `running`: a
function element without a
concluded record is executed again, which is safe because it has no effect; a `read`
element without one is sent again; an operation element of another class with
neither a concluded record nor an EffectAttempt was never sent and is advanced
as if reached for the first time — an approved, unused approval covers it
only while the rebuilt request has its `request_digest` (A10 rules 1 and 7).
judgement.why: P7 already decides that effectful operation work is durably marked before sending and becomes an unknown outcome on recovery rather than being silently repeated.

precedent.topic: Durable marker identifying an unrecorded execution for recovery
quotes:
Everything a resume or a restart needs is in the store before it is acted on:
   records of concluded attempts, decided approvals, and in-flight attempts before
   their request (K-17).

On start, before the surface accepts a request, the kernel turns every
`in_flight` EffectAttempt into `unknown` (A11 rule 4) and then derives every
run that has not ended — `running`, `awaiting_approval` or `pending` — again
from its records, oldest first in store order, rewriting a stored status or
waiting point that lags them (a decided approval, a resolved attempt, an
outcome whose run change was lost), and advances, as the
kernel actor, every run that derivation leaves `running`: a
function element without a
concluded record is executed again, which is safe because it has no effect; a `read`
element without one is sent again; an operation element of another class with
neither a concluded record nor an EffectAttempt was never sent and is advanced
as if reached for the first time — an approved, unused approval covers it
only while the rebuilt request has its `request_digest` (A10 rules 1 and 7).
precedent.why: State 2 identifies effect work with a pre-send EffectAttempt and identifies replayable function/read work from the durable run graph and absence of a concluded record.

topics.topic: Scope of state and observable effects discarded after a refused function trace write
questions: What exactly does “it has no effect” mean: no external service effect, no durable kernel-state change, no observable output from the abandoned attempt, or no difference between the abandoned execution and its retry?
Does “leaves none” mean only that no trace record exists, or that the function’s output and every kernel-stored edge value from that attempt are atomically discarded as well?

quotes:
A call that fails writes and changes no record; the only
trace it can leave is a published file no record names, which nothing reads:
a spooled file is replaced at its position, value bytes are reused by equal
bytes until the next start removes them (rule 4).

A non-empty list has no
record of its own: the elements' NodeExecutions are its durable facts, and
the list — its StoredValue identity, its files, its class — is derived from
them in element order whenever it is delivered, after a restart too, and
then named by every record that receives it.
judgement.why: P5 already decides that an unrecorded function attempt has no deliverable result and that any orphaned bytes are unnamed and unreadable.

precedent.topic: Visibility, retention, and cleanup of outputs and artifacts from an unrecorded execution
quotes:
A call that fails writes and changes no record; the only
trace it can leave is a published file no record names, which nothing reads:
a spooled file is replaced at its position, value bytes are reused by equal
bytes until the next start removes them (rule 4).

A non-empty list has no
record of its own: the elements' NodeExecutions are its durable facts, and
the list — its StoredValue identity, its files, its class — is derived from
them in element order whenever it is delivered, after a restart too, and
then named by every record that receives it.
precedent.why: State 2 makes concluded records the delivery facts and makes an orphaned file unreadable, replaceable or removable, so an unrecorded output cannot be delivered as a concluded result.

topics.topic: Whether function outputs may be published before the trace record is durable
questions: Must the function's output and node completion remain invisible until its immutable trace record is durably written, or may output be delivered to dependants before the trace write succeeds?
Must a function's trace record be durable before its output can be exposed to dependent nodes, or may dependants act on the output before the record write succeeds?

topics.topic: Required handling of nondeterministic output differences during function recovery
questions: When an admitted function is actually nondeterministic, does a trace-store refusal permit recovery to produce and accept a different output, or must recovery detect or prevent that difference for the claim that the abandoned execution “has no effect” to hold?

quotes:
Every concluded attempt at an element, every skipped node and every
`upstream_failed` node writes exactly one NodeExecution M23 — an owner's
resolution of an unknown outcome writes none (A11).

On start, before the surface accepts a request, the kernel turns every
`in_flight` EffectAttempt into `unknown` (A11 rule 4) and then derives every
run that has not ended — `running`, `awaiting_approval` or `pending` — again
from its records, oldest first in store order, rewriting a stored status or
waiting point that lags them (a decided approval, a resolved attempt, an
outcome whose run change was lost), and advances, as the
kernel actor, every run that derivation leaves `running`: a
function element without a
concluded record is executed again, which is safe because it has no effect;
judgement.why: P10 already decides that only the replay which obtains a concluded NodeExecution is authoritative, even if it differs from the abandoned execution.

precedent.topic: Authoritative result and evidence when replay produces a different result
quotes:
Every concluded attempt at an element, every skipped node and every
`upstream_failed` node writes exactly one NodeExecution M23 — an owner's
resolution of an unknown outcome writes none (A11).

On start, before the surface accepts a request, the kernel turns every
`in_flight` EffectAttempt into `unknown` (A11 rule 4) and then derives every
run that has not ended — `running`, `awaiting_approval` or `pending` — again

outcome whose run change was lost), and advances, as the
kernel actor, every run that derivation leaves `running`: a
function element without a
concluded record is executed again, which is safe because it has no effect;
precedent.why: Only the recovered attempt that obtains a concluded NodeExecution becomes authoritative; the unrecorded attempt supplies no durable evidence.

topics.topic: Trigger, timing, and observable durable status of the function recovery lifecycle
questions: What initiates this recovery, when does it run, and what durable run or node status is observable between the refused trace write and the replacement execution?

quotes:
On start, before the surface accepts a request, the kernel turns every
`in_flight` EffectAttempt into `unknown` (A11 rule 4) and then derives every
run that has not ended — `running`, `awaiting_approval` or `pending` — again
from its records, oldest first in store order, rewriting a stored status or
waiting point that lags them (a decided approval, a resolved attempt, an
outcome whose run change was lost), and advances, as the

function element without a
concluded record is executed again, which is safe because it has no effect; a `read`

neither a concluded record nor an EffectAttempt was never sent and is advanced

A store failure can leave a run's stored status behind its records. Any

judgement.why: State 2 makes recovery automatic at process start before requests are accepted and says the durable stored status may temporarily lag until startup derivation rewrites it.
